items.length: Paste 200–500 words for the best balance — too little produces sparse output, too much causes the AI to over-generalise.
items.numbers: Include statistics and numbers in your text — the AI highlights them prominently in the infographic.
items.summarize: Use the Summarizer first to condense very long documents, then feed the summary into the Infographic Generator.
items.edit: SVGs can be edited in Figma or Illustrator to adjust colours, fonts, or layout after generation.

how.question: How is the infographic generated?
how.answer: The AI structures your text into a spec — title, intro, statistics, sections, and conclusion — and the infographic is then rendered deterministically from that spec as an SVG. Text stays sharp and readable, with none of the garbled lettering typical of AI image generators.

input.question: What input works best?
input.answer: Factual text with clear points and a few numbers or statistics. A paragraph or two about a topic with concrete facts produces a much better layout than a one-line prompt.

edit.question: Can I edit the result?
edit.answer: The output is SVG, so you can open it in any vector editor (Figma, Inkscape, Illustrator) to tweak colors, text, or layout after downloading.

cost.question: How much does an infographic cost?
cost.answer: 2 image tokens per generation. Failed generations are refunded automatically.

style.question: Why does it not look like a photo or illustration?
style.answer: By design. This tool produces clean, data-focused layouts rather than pictorial art, because spec-based rendering guarantees legible text and consistent structure.
